# pysmelly — Code Smell Review Guide (Short)

> Generated by `pysmelly init --short`. Regenerate any time with that command.
> Full guidance: https://github.com/borwickatuw/pysmelly#readme

pysmelly performs **cross-file call-graph analysis** to find vestigial code
patterns that single-file linters (ruff, pylint) cannot detect.

## Severity

- **HIGH**: Fix these. Dead code, unused defaults, unreachable code.
- **MEDIUM**: Fix unless there's a specific reason not to (framework convention,
  public API). State the reason if you skip.
- **LOW**: Review and fix where it makes sense.

## Key principles

- **Default is to fix**, not to explain why the code is acceptable.
- **Do not dismiss findings by defending code in isolation** — the smell is in
  the cross-file picture (caller counts, blast radius), not the function itself.
- **Work incrementally**: fix top 1–2 highest severity, commit, re-run.

## Quick reference

```bash
uvx pysmelly                           # analyze current directory
uvx pysmelly --check dead-code         # single check
uvx pysmelly --diff main              # only findings in changes since main
uvx pysmelly git-history               # evolutionary/git history checks
```

Suppress a false positive: `x = 1  # pysmelly: ignore[check-name]`

Configure via `.pysmelly.toml` or `[tool.pysmelly]` in `pyproject.toml`.

# s3-bagit — findings register and review conventions

Run `make pysmelly` (repo root). The target invokes the globally
installed uv tool as `pysmelly . --more-please` (every finding, non-zero
exit on any) — fleet convention, and running
from the root is what lets repo config load (the generated quick
reference above says `uvx pysmelly`; the Makefile target is canonical
here). `pyproject.toml` carries a `[tool.pysmelly]` `tests/` exclude
(fleet family `fileplan-meta:81`, landed 2026-09-22): `src/` is
analyzed with stock settings, `tests/` is not analyzed at all.

## Regenerating this file

The generated preamble above ends by saying to regenerate any time with
`pysmelly init --short`. **Do not run that against this path.** The command
rewrites the *whole file*, not just the block it generated, so it takes
the findings register below — the baseline table, "Live state" and every
Phase 68 subphase record — with it. Verified by running it against a scratch
copy of the tree: the file came back as the bare generated stub with nothing
of this repo's register left. The command is only safe against a path nothing
has appended to.

Safe procedure, for when pysmelly reports the guidance is outdated:

```bash
pysmelly init --short "$(mktemp -d)/PYSMELLY.md"   # regenerate somewhere else
```

Then splice by hand: replace everything in this file *above* the horizontal
rule with the regenerated file's contents, and leave everything below the
rule alone. Keep the `<!-- pysmelly-guidance ... -->` marker line — pysmelly's
staleness check only looks for that hash string somewhere in the file, which
is what makes the partial splice sufficient. Regenerating to a scratch path
leaves the existing `CLAUDE.md` reference untouched (init matches any path
and stops), but check `git status` afterwards.

`tests/test_docs_references.py` fails if the register below the rule ever
goes missing, so a clobbering regeneration cannot pass `make check` quietly.

## s3-bagit's convention

**Near-zero suppression**, matching the other fleet repos. Findings
are fixed, or left standing as an operator-visible decision recorded in
the table below. Inline `# pysmelly: ignore` is reserved for cut-and-dry
false positives, each with a rationale and a `re-evaluate-by:` tag.
Whole-category `skip` config is not used for production code.

No inline ignores existed at onboarding. Two exist at HEAD — both added
in Phase 68d, both with a rationale and a `re-evaluate-by:` tag. See
"Live state" below.

## Suppression placement

The generated preamble teaches the trailing form
(`x = 1  # pysmelly: ignore[check-name]`). That form is not used here and is
superseded by this rule:

- The directive goes on **a full line of its own, directly above the finding
  line** — never trailing the finding.
- Append `# noqa: ERA001`: ruff's eradicate rule parses a bare
  `ignore[check-name]` line as commented-out code.
- Rationale and the `re-evaluate-by:` tag go on their own lines *above* the
  directive, which stays bare.

Trailing directives are black-unstable: a re-wrap moves the comment off the
line pysmelly checks and the suppression dies silently while still looking
present. Both live ignores in this repo use the full-line form —
`grep -rn 'pysmelly: ignore' src/` lists them, and
`tests/test_docs_references.py` asserts the shape. See the fleet's
pysmelly review guide, "Suppression-comment placement", for the
exact window pysmelly checks and the fleet evidence behind the rule.

**32 findings**, the honest as-found state. This repo was registered in
the fleet inventory on 2026-08-13 and onboarded the same day
(fleet plan Phase 68). Onboarding installs the gate and
records the baseline; it does **not** adjudicate findings. **Nothing in
the table below has been triaged or operator-approved.**

Counts are pinned to the onboarding commit. Re-measure at HEAD before
starting any remediation subphase.

| Check                   |  Total |    src |  tests | Note                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | -----: | -----: | -----: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| duplicate-blocks        |     13 |      1 |     12 | Almost entirely test-side (bag-fixture construction repeated across verify cases) — a fixture question.     |
| temp-accumulators       |      5 |      0 |      5 | All in `tests/conftest.py`; mechanical comprehension conversions.                                           |
| long-function           |      4 |      4 |      0 | `_build_parser` 185L, `create_bag` 145L, `verify_against` 149L, `verify_bag` 136L — same four as the C901s. |
| unused-defaults         |      2 |      2 |      0 | HIGH: `issue.py` `build_issue_url` / `open_issue` `brief=None` — the single caller always passes it.        |
| pass-through-params     |      2 |      0 |      2 | `conftest.build_tar_gz` forwards `files` / `wrap_prefix` straight to `build_tar`.                           |
| stdlib-alternatives     |      2 |      2 |      0 |                                                                                                             |

pysmelly also reports 2 convergence hotspots (informational; not counted
in the 32).

Compared with s3-archive's 99, this repo is small and the findings
cluster tightly: the four long functions are the four C901 acceptances,
and 19 of 32 are test-side scaffolding.

**Two of that table's characterizations turned out to be wrong.** The
`long-function` note ("same four as the C901s") is corrected in Phase
68e; the `duplicate-blocks` note ("bag-fixture construction repeated
across verify cases") is corrected in Phase 68b. Read the baseline as
what was measured, not as a diagnosis.

## Live state

**Counts are not recorded here.** They are derivable, they move whenever a
test lands, and drifting them is how this section went stale before (see
the R7 row below). Derive the current state instead:

```bash
make pysmelly              # full finding list, repo config loaded
pysmelly . --summary       # counts per check
```

`make pysmelly` reports zero findings as of the `[tool.pysmelly]` `tests/`
exclude (family `fileplan-meta:81`, 2026-09-22): every finding this
repo ever stood on was `duplicate-blocks` in `tests/`, and the tool no
longer analyzes that tree at all. **No `src/` finding is left standing
here**: if `make pysmelly` reports one it is new, and the disposition is
to fix it and write a row in the adjudication record below.

### git-history findings

`make pysmelly` does not run the history checks, so a finding can stand
here without ever appearing in the target's output. Derive them:

```bash
pysmelly git-history
```

One stands: `growth-trajectory` on `src/s3_bagit/cli.py`. SB-P4
(2026-09-18) moved the argparse-construction layer out into
`_cli_parsers.py`, which cut the module down and the reported growth with
it, but the check reads a six-month window and keeps reporting the
pre-split history until that window rolls past it. **Leave standing** —
the residual describes history, not present shape, and the one command
that would clear it (`pysmelly git-history reviewed`) resets the window
rather than answering the finding. `re-evaluate-by:` the second
comprehensive review after 2026-09.

### Standing decisions

Keyed by **test class**, not by count or line number. The classes are
stable; `duplicate-blocks` renumbers and regroups its pairs on every
edit, which is what makes a recorded count rot.

| Location                                                          | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tests/test_verify.py::TestCollectAllErrors`                      | **Leave standing** (Phase 68c, extended by R7). This is the 68f collect-all-errors gate. Each case spells out its own arrange and names the defect it pins, so a reviewer can tell a legitimate can't-continue return from a fail-fast regression. Collapsing them costs exactly that. **Ratified 2026-09-21** by the operator (2026-09-18 comprehensive review, answer c11), R7's six extension included. |
| `tests/test_verify_against.py::TestCollectAllErrors`              | **Leave standing** — the same gate, target side. **Ratified 2026-09-21** (answer c11), R7's six extension included.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tests/test_verify_against.py::TestLegitimateEarlyReturns`        | **Leave standing** — the counterpart pins: the returns that *should* stop the pass before listing the target. Their shared `target_listing_spy` skeleton is what makes the three comparable. **Ratified 2026-09-21** (answer c11).                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `tests/test_cli.py::TestVerifyAgainstCommand` ↔ `::TestLsCommand` | **Leave standing** (Phase 68c). The match is coincidental: those two share nothing but the rc/capsys skeleton.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

`re-evaluate-by:` the second comprehensive review after 2026-09 — an
event, not a date, so it fires when someone is already reading this file.
Re-deciding means re-reading the gate, not re-counting: the question is
whether the gate still needs case-by-case explicitness, never whether the
number moved.

The first three rows carry the operator's ratification of 2026-09-21: the
2026-09-18 comprehensive review re-read the gate at its sites, recommended
keeping all of it standing, and answer c11 ratified that. **A scout reading
this table does not re-mint a unit for a ratified row** — it re-reads the
gate at the trigger above, or not at all. The fourth row (the coincidental
`test_cli` skeleton match) was not part of that answer and stands on its
Phase 68c record alone.

**Landed 2026-09-22:** answer b2's `[tool.pysmelly]` `tests/` exclude
(family `fileplan-meta:81`) is in `pyproject.toml`, and
`pysmelly . --summary` reports zero findings — every one of these rows was
test-side. The table above is now the record of why each class was left
standing when it was still live, not a description of live output; it
stays for that reason rather than getting pruned. If a future edit to
`[tool.pysmelly]` narrows or drops the `tests/` exclude, re-derive the
live state before trusting this table again.

### Inline suppressions

`grep -rn 'pysmelly: ignore' src/` lists them; both were added in Phase
68d and both carry `re-evaluate-by: 2026-11`. `_cli_parsers.py`
`stdlib-alternatives` (argparse, kept for cross-repo consistency with
s3-archive; the two CLIs are paired on purpose, [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md)
006\) and `__init__.py` `compat-shims` (a confirmed false
positive — `_version.py` is gitignored and written by hatch-vcs at build
time).

The `stdlib-alternatives` directive moved out of `cli.py` when the parser
layer split into `_cli_parsers.py`. That finding names both files and
suppresses only at its first-listed (anchor) location, which the split
moved — leaving the `cli.py` directive inert and the finding visibly
firing. Re-placing it, not adding one, is the fix (PYSMELLY-REVIEW
Practice #10, "ineffective non-anchor").

### Phase 68g — shared `_bagit_checks` module (2026-08-13)

Measured 29 at `5ffd8ec`, 27 after. Two findings **fixed by
deduplication**, neither by suppression:

| Check                   | Before | After | Disposition                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | -----: | ----: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| duplicate-blocks        |     18 |    17 | Fixed the one `src/` instance: `verify._list_bag_objects` ≡ `verify_against._list_target_objects` collapsed onto `_list_objects`.       |
| duplicate-except-blocks |      1 |     0 | Fixed: `_check_payload_oxum` and `_check_payload_oxum_against_target` were one function differing only in how the actuals were counted. |

`long-function` stayed at 3 by design. Both verifiers shrank (`verify_bag`
136L → 132L, `verify_against` 149L → 147L) but neither was going to clear
the threshold from the outside; internal decomposition is Phase 68h.

**Why every name in `_bagit_checks.py` is `_`-prefixed:** see
[DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 003.

Mint check before writing: pysmelly's own `_extract_all_signatures` /
`_find_param_clumps` run over the tree with the proposed signatures
injected — 16 → 19 signatures, **0 raw clumps either way**. Nothing was
minted; the run after the change confirms it.

### Phase 68h — decompose both verifiers (2026-08-13)

Measured 27 at `eb19535`, 25 after. One category moved, by
decomposition, not suppression:

| Check         | Before | After | Disposition                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | -----: | ----: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| long-function |      3 |     1 | Fixed: `verify_bag` 132L → 90L (C901 17 → 6, four helpers), `verify_against` 147L → 89L (C901 23 → 6, six helpers). `create_bag` 123L is the only one left. |

Everything else is unchanged: duplicate-blocks 17, unused-defaults 2,
pass-through-params 2, temp-accumulators 2, single-call-site 1,
duplicate-except-blocks 0, convergence hotspots 0.

**Correction to the 68g record: three pysmelly checks see private
functions.** `param-clumps` and `dict-as-dataclass` both take private
names, and so does `vestigial-params`, which walks `ctx.all_trees` with
no name filter at all. Every one of the ten helpers added in 68h is
`_`-prefixed *and* uses every parameter it declares; ruff's `ARG` rules
agree independently.

Mint check before writing, same method as 68g: 16 → 20 signatures,
**0 raw clumps either way**. That run is what rejected the obvious
shape. A single `_load_manifests(client, bucket, bag_prefix, objects, result)` in `verify.py` would have been the third signature carrying
`{client, bucket, result}` alongside `_verify_files_single_pass`, and
`_find_param_clumps`'s intersection phase fires at three occurrences of
a three-parameter subset. Splitting it into `_discover_manifest_names`
(no client) and `_parse_manifests` keeps the count at two.

### Phase 68a — `issue.py` (2026-08-13)

Measured 25 at `b112869`, 22 after. Three findings, one knot:

| Check            | Before | After | Disposition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | -----: | ----: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| unused-defaults  |      2 |     0 | Fixed. HIGH severity, and the *finding* was right while its suggested fix was not. `brief` is always passed, so the default is dead — but `s3-bagit issue` declares `nargs="?", default=None`, so a bare invocation passes a genuine `None`. Correct signature is `brief: str \| None` with no default: the default is dead weight, the `\| None` is load-bearing. Reading "make it required" as "make it `str`" would have introduced a bug. |
| single-call-site |      1 |     0 | Fixed. `build_issue_url` had zero callers outside its own module, so it is inlined into `open_issue`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Mint tail worth recording: inlining leaves `open_issue` at one parameter
and one production call site, which *looks* like a fresh
`single-call-site`. It does not fire — `check_single_call_site` skips
functions imported by another production file
(`helpers.py:341 is_imported_in_production_elsewhere`) and `cli.py:57`
imports it.

### Phase 68i — decompose `create_bag` (2026-08-13)

Measured 22 at `49288ed`, 21 after. `long-function` 1 → 0, clearing the
category and with it the last `src/` finding outside `duplicate-blocks`.

`create_bag` went 123L → 82L in three staged extractions. One was not
enough, as in every prior decomposition in this arc: pulling the
argument validation out is the obvious first move and lands at 115,
still over the 100 bar. The extraction that pays is
`_tar_streamed_to_s3`, a `@contextlib.contextmanager` wrapping the pipe,
the uploader thread and the streaming `w|gz` tar.

### Phase 68b — the tagmanifest entry point (2026-08-13)

Measured 21 at `5b64c7f`, 17 after.

| Check               | Before | After | Disposition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | -----: | ----: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| pass-through-params |      2 |     0 | Fixed. `build_tar` existed only as a target for the `build_tar_gz` shim and its `mode` knob was never exercised — s3-bagit's fixtures are gzip-only. Folded together. (s3-archive keeps both, because it genuinely builds plain and xz tars.) |
| temp-accumulators   |      2 |     0 | Fixed. Both loops in `make_bag_files` became comprehensions.                                                                                                                                                                                  |

**The onboarding characterization of the test-side `duplicate-blocks`
was wrong, and it is worth saying why.** The baseline table called them
"bag-fixture construction repeated across verify cases", which reads as
"the fixtures need work". They did not: `s3_client` already created both
buckets and `make_bag_files` / `build_*` were already shared by every
flagged block. The actual duplication was tests hand-re-implementing
`make_bag_files`'s **own** tagmanifest loop, verbatim, because
`make_bag_files` offered no "I mutated a tag file, rebuild the
tagmanifest" entry point. The fix is a public
`conftest.rebuild_tagmanifests` that `make_bag_files` itself calls, so
there is one loop instead of two. Generalizable: when duplication sits
in tests, check whether the shared helper is missing an entry point
before concluding the tests are sloppy.

Side effect: `make_bag_files` dropped under the C901 ceiling, so the last
complexity acceptance in the repo — and the only one that was ever in
`tests/` — is gone. See [HOWTO-SIMPLIFY.md](HOWTO-SIMPLIFY.md).

### Phase 68c — parametrize the act-and-assert shapes (2026-08-13)

Measured 17 at `5ca088c`, 8 after. `duplicate-blocks` only.

The governing rule was **parametrize, never merge**: every collapse is a
`@pytest.mark.parametrize` row, and `pytest --co -q` held at 118 across
the whole subphase, which is what proves no assertion was silently
dropped. Collapsed: eight single-defect `verify_bag` bags, three
`verify_against` target-side defects, the three-format `ls` cluster, the
two `--strip-top-level` failure modes, and the ClientError wrap pair.
Fourteen ten-line positional `verify_against(...)` calls retired onto the
existing `_run_verify_against` wrapper, which 68f had defined below two
thirds of its potential callers.

**Four findings left standing on purpose**, and this is the durable part:
`test_verify.py::TestCollectAllErrors` (×2),
`test_verify_against.py::TestCollectAllErrors` and
`::TestLegitimateEarlyReturns`. Those are the 68f gate. Their
arrange/assert shapes are deliberately explicit — each spells out which
defect it pins, so a reviewer can tell a legitimate can't-continue return
from a fail-fast regression. Clearing a `duplicate-blocks` finding at the
cost of gate legibility is a bad trade. **Any future pass that proposes
to collapse them should stop.**

The gate was re-verified against the restructured tests in a throwaway
worktree by re-injecting three regressions:

| Injection                                                             | Tests failed |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -----------: |
| `return result` after the `bagit.txt is missing` fail in `verify_bag` |            1 |
| BagIt-Version `result.warn` upgraded to `result.fail`                 |            2 |
| `if not result.ok: return result` before `_reconcile_target_totals`   |            2 |

Every catch came from a gate test, not from a test 68c touched.

**Mint defence for test-side work, verified in pysmelly source.**
`param-clumps` (`structure.py:522`) and `dict-as-dataclass`
(`callers.py:1256`, `:1440`) both `continue` on `is_test_file` and
**cannot** fire on test code — the `src/`-side rule recorded in 68g/68h
inverts here. The live risks are `pass-through-params` (the
`build_tar_gz` finding 68b cleared is the standing proof),
`trivial-wrappers` (`patterns_data.py:265` — no `is_test_file` guard and
no nested-function guard), and `orphaned-test-helpers`, whose
`build_test_function_index` does **not** skip `_`-prefixed names, so a
private module-level helper with zero callers still mints.
`single-call-site` cannot fire in tests at all: it counts only
non-test call sites, so a test-only helper has zero and is skipped.
**Rule: `_`-prefix every new test helper, or make it a
`@pytest.fixture`.**

One reporting caveat, hit repeatedly across this arc: `duplicate-blocks`
reports one **pair** per group, not the full group. Fixing a reported
pair can surface a group sibling as an apparent mint that was really a
pre-existing duplicate. A `duplicate-blocks` count is a lower bound on
the duplication, not a measure of it.

### R7 — the two-entry gate cases (2026-08-17)

Measured 8 at `9dcc829`, 14 after `670b28c`. Not a pysmelly subphase — a
gate repair, recorded here because it moved the count.

Phase 68h invented a seventh injectable regression, R7:
`_map_expected_by_target` abandoning its walk after the first "entry
outside `data/`" error instead of collecting and continuing. All 118
tests passed it, because no bag in the repo carried **two** misplaced
manifest entries, so "stop after the first" and "collect them all" were
indistinguishable. `670b28c` added one two-entry case per verifier:

- `test_verify_against.py::TestCollectAllErrors::test_two_manifest_entries_outside_data_are_both_reported`
- `test_verify.py::TestCollectAllErrors::test_two_misplaced_payload_entries_are_both_reported`

| Check            | Before | After | Disposition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | -----: | ----: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| duplicate-blocks |      8 |    14 | **Left standing**, all six gate-side. Each new case pair-matches the neighbours it sits beside in `TestCollectAllErrors`. That is the trade Phase 68c already made on the record for this gate, extended to two more cases — not a new adjudication, a wider one. |

Attribution is reproducible: `git log -S'<test name>' -- tests/` returns
`670b28c` for both names, and re-measuring the commit against its parent
reproduces the 8 → 14 step.

**The decision was taken; it was taken in the wrong place.** `670b28c`'s
commit message states the 8 → 14 and the reasoning in full. Nobody
reading `docs/PYSMELLY.md` can see a commit message, so this register
said 8 while the tool said 14 — and the next session's first move would
have been to re-derive, or re-litigate, a call already made. That is what
the widened rule above is for, and it is why the "Live state" section
above now carries the derivation command instead of a number.

### SB-P5 — the extract-flow report assertions (2026-09-18)

Measured 14 at `8247564`, 11 after. `duplicate-blocks` only; three
findings, all in `tests/test_cli.py` and all **outside** the 68f gate —
`TestExtractThenVerify` ↔ `TestExtractArchiveWrap`,
`TestExtractArchiveWrap` ↔ `TestExtractStripTopLevel` (twice). What they
shared was the act-and-assert skeleton: `assert rc == N`, then
`captured = capsys.readouterr()`, then `assert "RESULT: VALID|INVALID" in captured.out`, then each case's own report fragments.

The only thing standing over them was this register's own sentence that
collapsing them "would cost more legibility than it buys" — a prior
session's self-assessment, which PYSMELLY-REVIEW Practice #8 weights at
about zero. Drafting the fix showed the sentence was defending the wrong
thing: what makes the wrap pair legible is that the two cases assert
*opposite* outcomes, and that contrast lives in the expectations, not in
the six lines of skeleton around them.

Fixed by a module-level `_assert_extract_report(capsys, rc, *, valid, contains=(), absent=())`. `valid` carries the whole verdict (rc 0 with
`RESULT: VALID`, rc 1 with `RESULT: INVALID` — one CLI contract, not a
per-test fact); `contains` / `absent` stay per-test, so each caller still
names its own fragments and the opposite-outcome pair still reads as
opposites at the call site. Nothing was merged and no
`@pytest.mark.parametrize` row was created: 68c's "parametrize, never
merge" rule holds, and `pytest --co -q` held at 139 across the change.
The `--no-verify` case keeps its explicit `"RESULT:" not in` assertion —
it claims the absence of a verdict, which is a different claim from
either verdict.

Mint defence, per 68c's test-side rule: the helper is `_`-prefixed and
has six callers, so `orphaned-test-helpers` (which does not skip private
names) cannot fire; it is non-trivial — it does the `readouterr`, the
verdict selection and both assertion loops — so `trivial-wrappers`
(no `is_test_file` guard) does not either. Confirmed by the run: no new
check appears, and the `contains` / `absent` loop shape it adopts is the
one `test_client_error_is_wrapped` already used in the same file.

The `TestVerifyAgainstCommand` ↔ `TestLsCommand` pair from the same 68c
row is untouched and still standing: that one is a coincidental rc/capsys
match between two unrelated commands, not a shared report assertion.

#### Standing-suppression audit (PYSMELLY-REVIEW Practice #10)

Both layers checked against live output at the lane's HEAD.

- **Config-level skips: none.** There is no `[tool.pysmelly]` section in
  `pyproject.toml`, so there is no skip list to rot and no `exclude`
  silently replacing the tool's defaults.
- **Inline directives: both LIVE at their anchor, none dead, none
  drifted.** Verified by strip-audit, not by reading: the tree was copied
  with its `.git` (so `.gitignore` is honoured and `_version.py` raises no
  phantom finding), every `# pysmelly: ignore` line deleted in the copy,
  and the copy re-run. Each stripped directive brought back exactly one
  finding at exactly its annotated site — `compat-shims` in `__init__.py`,
  `stdlib-alternatives` in `_cli_parsers.py` — and the
  `duplicate-blocks` set was identical in both runs.
- **Placement: correct at both sites.** Each directive is a bare full line
  at `finding.line - 1` with its rationale above it, which is the
  black-stable form this file's "Suppression placement" section requires.
- **Both within their window.** `re-evaluate-by: 2026-11` on each; the
  rationales were re-read against the code this run and both still hold.
  `_cli_parsers.py`'s cross-repo argument is corroborated rather than
  asserted — the same module imports `validate_profile_name` from
  `s3_archive`, so the pairing is real.
- **Nothing added and nothing removed.** No removal is proposed.

#### Raised, not taken

Follow-ups the lane surfaced and deliberately left for the operator:

- `make pysmelly` shows only the first ten findings; the target does not
  pass `--more-please`, so the on-demand view is truncated by default.
- A `--min-severity high` gate inside `make check` is available (that band
  is empty here) but wiring it in contradicts the fleet's on-demand
  decision, so SB-P6 recorded the rationale instead of adding the gate.
- `tests/test_docs_references.py` carries the literal string
  `pysmelly: ignore` inside its own assertions. pysmelly's suppression
  scan is raw text over a three-line window, so those literals parse as
  blanket ignores. Measured inert today — the finding set is identical
  with them neutralized — but it is a latent suppression inside the file
  whose job is to police suppressions.
- The same file's placement check walks `src/` only, and its `check:`
  prerequisite guard does not notice pysmelly being wired into `lint:`,
  which `check` depends on.
